findings.reason: a worker placing "every one of its live names" must reconcile against one count, and 37 missing names or a wrong 47 % sends the division at the wrong population.
findings.text: §6 states `transport` holds 1,042 live names on the 2026-11-17 reading with 47 % carrying a domain among their sources', while §2:33 in the same plan states 1,079 and 530 of 1,079 (49 %), and a bounded live read on 2026-11-17 reproduces §2 exactly (3,267 live names, 1,079 with domain `transport`, 530 agreeing out of 1,079, 1,058 carrying any source domain); §6 never says which population its 1,042 excludes, so the count a worker must place every live name against is ambiguous and the refused-split justification (197 names into a 17-name group) rests on a reading nothing records

findings.reason: without a planted name the section's sole verification cannot fail in the way it is meant to catch.
findings.text: §6's only measured check is "the count of names per part read back from the live graph equals the ruled proposal's", which compares the writer's own read against its own proposal with no planted name whose part is known and no reconciliation to the live transport count, so a placement or count query that silently matches nothing reads as exactly equal and correct; §2, §3, §4 and §6 of this plan each plant a control for their own guard, and §6 plants none

findings.reason: the ruled release route for `transport`'s parts needs a node that waits on §6, otherwise §5 can close with the parts never audited or cut.
findings.text: §2's ruling states "Its parts are released after the other groups", but §5 depends only on §4 and covers "each group in the order ruled in §2", while the parts and their names come from §6 (which depends only on §2); no edge or done-when makes any node audit, bar and cut the transport parts after §6 has created them, so the plan's stated release of a third of the catalog is unowned

findings.reason: a node repairing the first group cannot tell whether it is capped at USD 40 or USD 300, and the ruled raise is unreadable without a base.
findings.text: §2's ruling records "The repair ceiling is raised by USD 50 to USD 300" with no base figure anywhere in the plan, while §4's done-when still holds the first group to "the spend ceiling" and its release notes to "a ceiling of USD 40"; nothing states whether the raised ceiling replaces the per-group ceiling, bounds total repair spend, or leaves §4's USD 40 intact

findings.reason: the effort total is what a coordinator sizes and orders dispatches against, and it now disagrees with the sections that make it.
findings.text: `plan-effort-hours` still declares 30.0 while the declared sections now sum to 36.0 (6 + 4 + 6 + 8 + 6 + 6 after §6 was added), so the plan's own total understates the work by the new section's effort
